front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, instances fail the load balancer health checks but the group never replaces them. What do you change?
back: Turn on the ELB health check type for the group.
extra: For the [Elastic Load Balancing health checks](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-elb-check-must-be-turned-on) of a group, [you must turn it on](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-elb-check-must-be-turned-on).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, can one Auto Scaling group span two Regions?
back: No. It spans Availability Zones, not Regions.
extra: Auto Scaling groups are [regional constructs](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-regional-spans-azs-not-regions): they [can span Availability Zones, but not AWS regions](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-regional-spans-azs-not-regions).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, the load rises at the same known time every weekday. What adds capacity before it arrives?
back: A scheduled action.
extra: Scheduled scaling fits when [the need arises on a predictable schedule](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-vs-dynamic-when-to-use).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, the group must keep average CPU utilization near one value that you choose. Which policy type?
back: A target tracking scaling policy.
extra: You set a target value, and EC2 Auto Scaling [adjusts the number of EC2 instances](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-target-tracking-definition) to keep the metric near it.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, a worker group processes messages from an SQS queue. Which metric does it scale on?
back: Backlog per instance: queue length divided by InService instances.
extra: Use a [backlog per instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-sqs-backlog-per-instance) metric: [Divide that number by the fleet's running capacity](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-sqs-backlog-per-instance).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, can you hibernate an instance that is in an Auto Scaling group?
back: No. The group marks it unhealthy and can replace it.
extra: [You can't hibernate an instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-cannot-hibernate-group-instance) in a group. If you try, the service [marks the stopped instance as unhealthy](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-cannot-hibernate-group-instance).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, the default cooldown of an Auto Scaling group is {{c1::300 seconds}}.
extra: That is [5 minutes](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-default-cooldown-300-seconds).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, a group that you create with the AWS CLI has a default health check grace period of {{c1::0 seconds}}.
extra: In the console the default is [300 seconds](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-grace-period-console-300-cli-0).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, the default heartbeat timeout of a lifecycle hook is {{c1::3600 seconds}}.
extra: That is [1 hour](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-heartbeat-timeout-default).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, a predictive scaling policy starts to forecast after its metric has {{c1::at least 24 hours of data}}.
extra: A new group cannot get a forecast on its first day.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, Amazon EC2 can reclaim a Spot Instance of the group at any time with a {{c1::two-minute interruption notice}}.
extra: A lifecycle hook [does not prevent an instance from terminating](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-spot-two-minute-notice).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, without an instance maintenance policy, the minimum healthy percentage of an instance refresh is {{c1::90 percent}}.
In EC2 Auto Scaling, the maximum instance lifetime of a group must be at least {{c1::86,400 seconds}}.
extra: That is one day, so the fastest scheduled replacement is daily.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling behind a load balancer, Elastic Load Balancing waits {{c1::300 seconds}} by default to complete deregistration (connection draining).
extra: In-flight requests get this time when the group scales in.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, simple, step or target tracking policy: which one waits for the cooldown period between scaling activities?
back: Simple scaling policies.
extra: The group waits for the cooldown before further [scaling activities initiated by simple scaling policies](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-cooldown-applies-to-simple-scaling).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, a new AMI must reach every instance that already runs in the group. Which feature do you use?
back: An instance refresh with a new launch template version.
extra: For [Deploying a new Amazon Machine Image (AMI)](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-instance-refresh-use-cases), an instance refresh can [roll out the updates immediately](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-instance-refresh-use-cases).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, can you modify a launch configuration after you create it?
back: No. You create a new launch configuration instead.
extra: You [can't modify a launch configuration](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-launch-config-immutable) after you create it. A launch template has versions.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, one group must run both Spot and On-Demand Instances. What must the group launch from?
back: A launch template.
extra: A group takes [multiple purchase options](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-purchase-options-need-launch-template) [only when you use a launch template](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-purchase-options-need-launch-template).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, a mixed instances group adds Spot Instances. Which Spot allocation strategy does AWS recommend to start with?
back: Price-capacity-optimized.
extra: The [price and capacity optimized allocation strategy](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-spot-price-capacity-optimized-recommended) picks the pools [least likely to be interrupted](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-spot-price-capacity-optimized-recommended).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, does scale-in protection stop the group from replacing an instance that fails its health checks?
back: No. It protects the instance only against scale in.
extra: Scale-in protection [does not protect Auto Scaling instances](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-scale-in-protection-not-health-replacement) from [Health check replacement](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-scale-in-protection-not-health-replacement).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, an instance must save its work before scale in terminates it. What do you add to the group?
back: A termination lifecycle hook.
extra: The hook [extends the life of your Amazon EC2 instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-termination-hook-extends-life), so the work can move: [transfer the work to another instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-termination-hook-extends-life).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, does a termination lifecycle hook keep a Spot Instance running until its job ends?
back: No. Amazon EC2 still reclaims it after the notice.
extra: A lifecycle hook [does not prevent an instance from terminating](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-spot-two-minute-notice) after the [two-minute interruption notice](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-spot-two-minute-notice).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, oldest instance or outdated configuration: which one does the default termination policy remove first?
back: An instance with an outdated configuration, in the fullest zone.
extra: It first picks the zone that [has the most instances](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-termination-default-zone-with-most), then aims to [terminate instances that are using outdated configurations first](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-termination-default-outdated-first).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, does a predictive scaling policy on its own scale in when the forecast expects less load?
back: No. Add a dynamic policy, such as target tracking.
extra: If the forecast expects a decrease in load, [it will not scale in to remove capacity](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-predictive-does-not-scale-in).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, new instances need a long time to initialize, so scale out is slow. What do you add to the group?
back: A warm pool of pre-initialized instances.
extra: A warm pool is a [pool of pre-initialized EC2 instances](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pool-definition). For stopped instances in it, you [pay only for the volumes that you use](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pool-stopped-instances-pay-volumes-only) and attached Elastic IP addresses.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, does a new instance get the data of the instances that already run in the group?
back: No. Use a lifecycle hook to copy it.
extra: [Data is not automatically copied](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-data-not-copied-to-new-instances). You can use [lifecycle hooks to copy the data](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-data-not-copied-to-new-instances), or an Amazon RDS database.

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, software must be configured on a new instance before it gets load balancer traffic. What do you use?
back: A launch lifecycle hook.
extra: Lifecycle hooks act [before an instance goes into service](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-lifecycle-hooks-definition): [launch hooks can perform software configuration](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-lifecycle-hooks-definition).

front: EC2 Auto Scaling or AWS Auto Scaling: which one manages scaling for resources across several AWS services?
back: AWS Auto Scaling.
extra: Use AWS Auto Scaling for [multiple resources across multiple services](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-use-ec2-vs-aws-auto-scaling). Use EC2 Auto Scaling if you [only need to scale Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-use-ec2-vs-aws-auto-scaling) groups.

front: In AWS, an Amazon ECS service or a DynamoDB table must scale automatically. Which scaling service do you use?
back: Application Auto Scaling.
extra: To scale a resource other than EC2, [you can use the Application Auto Scaling API](../facts/aws-auto-scaling.md#aws-auto-scaling-faq-application-auto-scaling-for-non-ec2).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, can a target tracking policy scale out the group while the metric is below the target value?
back: No.
extra: Target tracking cannot scale out when the [metric is below the target value](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-target-tracking-no-scale-out-below-target).

front: In Amazon EC2 scaling, scale up or scale out: which one needs the instance stopped?
back: Scale up: you stop the instance to change its type.
extra: [You must stop your instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-vertical-stop-required) before you change its instance type, so you [plan for downtime](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-vertical-stop-required).

front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, you add an Availability Zone to a group behind a load balancer. What else must you change?
back: Enable that Availability Zone on the load balancer.
extra: Expansion means [adding an Availability Zone](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-add-az-group-and-load-balancer) to the group and [enabling that Availability Zone for your load balancer](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-add-az-group-and-load-balancer).
